newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end higher, rally pushes Dow over 7300.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end higher, rally pushes Dow over 7300.

text.p: U.S. stocks rallied on Thursday, with the Dow Jones industrial Average and the Standard & Poor's 500 Index moving to new record high closing levels as a late buying spree sent blue chips surging.

A wave of buying generated by a computer program accounted for most of the Dow's gains. The 30-stock average closed up 47 points or 0.65 percent to 7333, its first close above the 7,300 level ever. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index rose six to nearly 842, a new record.

Blue chip stocks had been saddled for most of the session in tight trading ranges amid mixed inflation signals, causing many to delay big investment decisions before a meeting on interest rates by the U.S. central bank next week.

The second leg of a government inflation report, the core Consumer Price Index, had stirred Wall Street's fears of inflation and a possible credit tightening at the May 20 meeting of Fed policy-makers.
April retail prices rose slightly higher than Wall Street expected, increasing 0.3 percent. Economists had forecast a rise of 0.2 percent, on average.
The U.S. Producer Price Index, released on Wednesday, had pointed to lower wholesale prices in April.

"We see a 50/50 chance that the Fed may raise rates just to continue with their pre-emptive strike but the inflation numbers have looked pretty good this week," said Elaine Garzarelli, who remains bullish with a year-end target of 7,600 for the Dow.
Traders said they were also waiting to see if there would be a new round of investment by the public in mutual funds.

AMG Data Services of Arcata, Calif. is expected to release data on Thursday on cash flowing into stock mutual funds for this week. Another firm, Mutual Fund Trim Tabs of Santa Rosa, Calif., is due to report its latest numbers on Friday.
The massive late buying program accounted for 35 points of the Dow's 47 point gain, according to Birinyi Associates Inc.
Technology stocks sizzled boosting the Nasdaq Composite Index 18 points to 1353. On a percent basis, its gain of 1.35 percent doubled the 0.65 percent rise in the Dow.

Internet bookseller Amazon.com Inc thundered onto the Nasdaq after the company's IPO market debut - the second high-profile technology IPO this week. Shares opened with a 60 percent gain but settled back to close up 5-1/2 to 23-1/2. Analysts said the scorching market debut could signal a turn in investor sentiment for technology IPOs.

Computer disk drive makers Western Digital Corp, Quantum Corp and Seagate Technology Inc all ended higher after Lehman Brothers and Soundview Financial Group Inc initiated coverage of the stocks with bullish recommendations.
The most-heavily traded Nasdaq stock was Informix Corp, rising 2-3/16 to 11-3/8 amid takeover rumors.

Gateway 2000 shares surged 7-1/2 to 68-7/8 after it set a stock split and said it would buy back up to ten million of its own shares. The personal computer marketer also said it will to the New York Stock Exchange on May 22.
Chrysler Corp shares slipped after the chief executive Robert Eaton said he May domestic car sales to be weaker than forecasts. The stock closed down 1/2 to 31-1/8.
Capital One Financial Corp shares fell 3-1/2 to 36-3/8 after the credit card issuer said it expects flat second quarter earnings, prompting two brokerage firms to cut their ratings of the stock.
Advancing stocks just nosed ahead of falling stocks by 1280 to 1165 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The S&P 500 rose 5.84 to 841.88, a new record.
The Nasdaq closed up 18.03 to 1353.58.
Volume on the NYSE was 458.1 million shares.
((-- Wall Street Desk, 212-859-1881))
